exposure: Di (2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) at 1 mM for 13 days
outcome: Antioxidant enzyme activities (Superoxide dismutase (SOD), Glutathione S-transferase (GST), Glutathione peroxidase (GPx), Catalase (CAT))
Gene expression (microsomal GST1, GST (k, m, th, o, and Z), 8-oxoguanine DNA glycosylase (OGG1), glutathione reductase (GR), nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2), GPx2, SOD3)
cohort: Skeletal muscle cells derived from human abdominal muscle biopsies (from healthy women undergoing planned cesarean surgery) and California sea lion samples (collected postmortem from stranded animals).
finding: DEHP exposure increased oxidative stress and phase two detoxification in human skeletal muscle cells, while activating antioxidant defenses to maintain redox homeostasis in California sea lion cells, demonstrating species-specific responses.
